Delhi's archaeology department offers 12 research fellowships in archaeology and conservation

The Department of Archaeology of the Delhi government is inviting applications for six senior and six junior research fellowships, paying Rs 50,000 and Rs 25,000 a month. Applicants must have lived in Delhi since 1 January 2022 or earlier, and applications must reach the department within 30 days of the advertisement, which ran on 11 November.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 24 November 2026

Where
Delhi
Apply by
10 December 2026

The Department of Archaeology of the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi has advertised its new Research Fellowship scheme. The scheme was notified in the Delhi Gazette on 15 October 2026, following a cabinet decision of 29 June 2026, and the department posted the advertisement, the application form and the gazette notification on its website on 11 November.

There are 12 fellowships, all listed in the advertisement as unreserved, though the gazette says OBC, SC, ST, EWS and PwD candidates get preference in selection under the usual rules: three Senior Research Fellowships (SRF) and three Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) in archaeology, and the same in conservation. An SRF pays Rs 50,000 a month and a JRF Rs 25,000, subject to TDS. The term is one year from joining, which can be extended by one more year for outstanding fellows on the monitoring committee's recommendation and with official approval.

For archaeology, an SRF needs a PhD in Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology or in History, with a postgraduate diploma in archaeology as a desirable extra; a JRF needs a master's in ancient or medieval Indian history or in archaeology. For conservation, an SRF needs a PhD in conservation, preservation or heritage management, with a postgraduate diploma in conservation desirable; a JRF needs a master's in conservation, preservation and heritage management or in conservation. The upper age limit is 40 on the last date for applying.

The scheme is meant for residents of Delhi, and applicants must send proof of residence in Delhi since 1 January 2022 or earlier. They must not be in government service or receiving any other fellowship, scholarship or grant from a central or state government or public body. The fellowship is full-time work and gives no claim to a regular job, a person may apply only once, and research proposals should look at the history of Delhi's lesser-known monuments. The gazette says the department will hold the copyright of published work, and a fellow who leaves before the year is out must repay the stipend with 12 per cent annual interest.

Applications are on paper only. Besides certificates of education, category and any experience listed on the form, the packet includes the prescribed form, a research synopsis of no more than three A4 pages, a statement of no more than 1,000 words on the topic and its value to the applicant's career, up to two letters of recommendation, copies of PAN and Aadhaar cards, an undertaking, and a bank draft of Rs 500 (Rs 250 for OBC, SC, ST, EWS, PwD and women candidates) in favour of the DDO, Department of Archaeology, GNCTD. It goes to the Head of Office (Archaeology) at Vikas Bhawan-II, Civil Lines, Delhi. Shortlisted candidates are interviewed.

The advertisement prints no calendar closing date. It says applications must reach the department within 30 days of its publication, and the copy on the department's website is from the Navbharat Times of 11 November 2026, which puts the end of that window at about 10 or 11 December, depending on how the days are counted. Since applications must arrive, not merely be posted, by then, it is safer to send them early; applicants who are unsure can check with the department by phone or at deptt-ofarchaeology@delhi.gov.in.
